snippets.output: Muscle strain, also known as muscle pull or muscle tear, is a common injury that occurs when a muscle is stretched or torn, causing pain, stiffness, and limited mobility.
The duration of muscle strain pain can vary depending on the severity of the injury and the individual's overall health.
The pain from muscle strain can last from a few days to several weeks or even months.
Mild muscle strain may resolve within 1-3 days, moderate strain may take 7-14 days to heal, and severe strain may take longer than 14 days to recover.
Most people can expect to recover from mild muscle strain within 1-2 weeks, but some muscle strains may take longer to heal and may require medical attention.
The severity of muscle strain can be classified into three stages: acute (0-24 hours), sub-acute (24-72 hours), and chronic (beyond 72 hours).

A study published in the Journal of Pain classified the severity of muscle strain. The accuracy of expected pain intensity increased during the study, with actual pain intensity accounting for up to 55% of the variance in expected pain intensity.
